script.base: Spread and total are not saved, so this is a form script only. JAX's engine is Bhayshul Tuten on the ground (28 carries, 131 yards; 66 and 65) and Parker Washington downfield (18 targets, 181 yards, 279 air), with Brian Thomas Jr the WR2 (11 targets, 80 yards, 126 air). NE splits rushes among Rhamondre Stevenson (24/94; 51 and 43), TreVeyon Henderson (16/76, one listed game) and Drake Maye (9/67) and splits targets across Demario Douglas (9/29), Stevenson (8/47), Hunter Henry (8/66), Mack Hollins (7/69) and Romeo Doubs (7/96, 151 air). Base case is a competitive game in which Tuten and Stevenson both keep double-digit carries and neither offense has to abandon the run.
script.flip1: NE's 38% blitz gets home on a JAX offense at -0.40 EPA/dropback when blitzed versus +0.42 when not. Lawrence checks down, Washington and Thomas air yards stall, and if JAX trails Tuten's carry share shrinks toward Chris Rodriguez (12/36) and Ameer Abdullah (7/43).
script.flip2: Dre'Mont Jones (out) and Quintayvious Hutchins (out) mean the blitz never arrives, Brenden Schooler (out) and Craig Woodson (questionable) leave the deep middle thin, Washington repeats an 80-plus yard day, NE falls behind, Maye throws, and Stevenson/Henderson rush yards die late while Doubs, Hollins and Henry targets rise.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game nflverse report, not the 90-minute inactives: JAX DT Albert Regis Doubtful (elbow) — if he sits, NE interior runs (Stevenson, Henderson, Maye) face an unnamed backup; no JAX offensive skill player is out. NE LB Dre'Mont Jones Out (shoulder) and LB Quintayvious Hutchins Out (knee) remove a pass rusher and a coverage linebacker, which weakens the blitz that has crushed JAX (-0.40 EPA/db) and helps JAX TE Brenton Strange, RB dumps and the slot. NE S Brenden Schooler Out (back) and S Craig Woodson Questionable (shoulder) thin the deep middle in front of Washington and Thomas. NE TE Eli Raridon Questionable (thigh) is absent from the two-week target list (Henry 8 targets, L. Larison 2), so a scratch does not move the TE target. No same-position offensive teammate has a stale line to promote.

matchup.shell: No man/zone or MOFO/MOFC charting in the pack. Location splits only: JAX allows 19.0 YPA on 7 middle attempts, 7.86 left (28) and 7.78 right (18). NE allows 10.69 YPA middle (13), 4.48 left (23) and 5.18 right (28). Both middle spikes are small samples; the attempt volume is outside.
matchup.pressure: JAX blitz rate 39%; NE EPA/db is +0.09 vs blitz and -0.06 vs none, and Maye has 9 carries for 67 rush yards, so pressure has not shut NE down. NE blitz rate 38%; JAX EPA/db is -0.40 vs blitz and +0.42 vs none — the sharpest clash in the pack — but Jones being out is why that pressure edge may not travel.
matchup.bleeds: JAX bleeds the middle (19.0 YPA, n=7) and explosives (8 passes of 20+ on 58 attempts) with a middling run defense (4.13 YPC, 5 runs of 10+). NE bleeds the middle on a small sample (10.69 YPA, n=13) but has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ on 70 attempts, so explosives have been capped; run defense is 4.30 YPC with 5 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: JAX's primary, Washington (18 targets, 279 air), does not cleanly overlap a defense that has limited 20+ passes (4/70) even with Schooler out — that conflict is why he is not a leg. The usable overlap is carry share into average run defenses: Tuten 28/131 into NE's 4.30 YPC, Stevenson 24/94 into JAX's 4.13 YPC with Regis doubtful. NE has no single primary receiver on JAX's middle bleed (Douglas leads targets at 9 but has 29 yards; Doubs has the air, 151, on a 0-and-96 split).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both rush overs lost because the unsaved spread was a real number. One team led by two scores, the trailer emptied the run game, and two-week floors were the trap. Tuten's 66 and 65 came with a 14-carry script he did not get once JAX trailed; Rodriguez took the hurry-up scraps and Tuten finished near 40. Stevenson lost the efficient carries to Henderson and to Maye scrambles against a 39% JAX blitz, Regis played through the doubtful tag, and 9 carries at a stuffed YPC landed under 35. With no saved price there was also no CLV check, so the market may already have known the script we could not see.
slip_story: One competitive-game run stack only: Tuten rushyds over 52 with Stevenson rushyds over 35. They win together if neither side abandons the run and lose together in a shootout or a one-sided chase — do not add Washington, Thomas or Doubs overs, a total under, any TD, or a second market on either back. If a posted spread or the inactives show a blowout lean, the human should cut the stack as script-dependent. No bet is placed.
